glomeris resource — Manage ownership and reclaim enrolled generated artifacts.

usage: glomeris resource <operation> [operation arguments]

Safety depends on the subcommand; each is labelled below. The strongest of
them: Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.

Glomeris-created source-free compiler artifacts only. Acquiring owners hold a
shared barrier; retirement holds it exclusively and uses the existing policy
and executor. Default inactivity is 24 hours since meaningful use, not lease
renewal. Existing unknown worktrees and user data are never enrolled. All
operations render JSON; unattended sweep requires explicit per-class policy.

Subcommands
  create --source-root <workspace> --recipe <recipe>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Create one private generation with committed reconstruction source.
  produce <id> <generation> --input <tracked-rs-file>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Create a bounded standalone compiler object from retained committed
      input; reject external/environment dependencies.
  hold <id> <generation> --host <host> --session <session> --owner-pid <pid>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Persist acquisition and hold a shared kernel barrier through native
      use.
  seal <id> <generation>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Verify source-free compiler outputs after all consumers release.
  inspect
      Read-only, and runs installed build tools to locate their caches.
      Read lifecycle and safety blockers; no resource mutation.
  reconcile
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Recover persisted intent without repeating destructive actions.
  sweep --unattended
      Can delete data — every deletion is policy-gated.
      Execute only enrolled, independently verified, policy-authorized
      generations.
  authority <apply|grant-managed> --expected-current <snapshot>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      CAS-update the existing Autopilot authority without overwriting
      intervening changes.
  policy <show|apply file>
      Writes only Glomeris's own state — never your files.
      Inspect or CAS-update per-class retention; authorization still
      requires the existing Autopilot envelope.

See also: daemon, actions
